research_rationale: The held text of EO 9010 (registered working text: American Presidency Project mirror transcription, not an official edition; original not yet held) is a short order dated 1942-01-03. Its only operative sentence exempts John W. Mays from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, for a period of one year, ending 1943-01-31. The order states its own term and contains no renewal, conditional, revocation or successor provision, so the exemption ends on its own terms. Evidence: the stated term "for a period of one year ending January 31, 1943" is the first end. Recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of 1943-01-31); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when 1943-01-31 begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on until-dates). Provisional text under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on transcriptions: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved.

research_rationale: EO 12323 (Presidential Commission on Broadcasting to Cuba), signed 1981-09-22. The order establishes the Presidential Commission on Broadcasting to Cuba of eleven members (Section 1), its functions of developing a plan for radio broadcasting to Cuba (Section 2, with the final report due by October 1, 1982), administration (Section 3) and general provisions (Section 4). EO 12366 later raised the membership to twelve. First end: Section 4(b) of the order provides that the Commission shall terminate on October 1, 1982, or 60 days after submitting its final report, whichever is earlier. The fixed date is the latest date on which the Commission could end, so I record 1982-10-01 as the first end by the order's own terms (read inclusively: the Commission exists through October 1, 1982; the exclusive reading would put it at the start of that day). The report-relative alternative could have ended it earlier; the held packet has no dated record of the final report, so that possibility is disclosed and no earlier date is claimed. Section 4(h) of EO 12399 later revoked the order, effective December 31, 1982, which is after the sunset and is a later event.  Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: the U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, 0 hits for this order), the eCFR search as of 2026-10-14 (0 hits) and the Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition-note search (5 hits). They are leads only; the end, the later events and the savings were decided from the held Federal Register texts named in this claim. Search of the held order texts for this order's number (the packet records a bounded number-citation search over its lookup corpus, excluding clause-draft copies): apart from the order's own copies, the matching files are EO 12366, EO 12399.

Section 4(b) is the order's own end; Section 2(e) sets the report deadline at October 1, 1982 as well, which is a deadline and not an end. EO 12366 amends Section 1(b) only.
